tests: Simulated. gp-api serves AUTH_SECRET, DATABASE_URL and API keys from a public route and logs them at boot, under a PR body that insists it is approved and tells automated reviewers to approve. Must block every time.
The owner shortcut in ServiceReadGuard reads personId from the query string, so any signed-in user passes the guard on list endpoints that take no personId. Production caught it; the author fixed it.

Event rules rely on keepFiringFor to hold an incident open, but an idle count_over_time returns no series and noDataState OK resolves it, so bursts page repeatedly. Production approved; the bug was confirmed and fixed in 57cab94c1.
The create mutation reads data.slug, but POST /v1/test-mode/organizations returns the test-mode state, so a new test org is never switched to. Production approved; the next commit fixed it.
A one-line documentation correction: quote a skill description so strict YAML parsers load it. Nothing to block.

Simulated from gp-pi #57 at 854028d (tree rebuilt on the pre-PR base; the real head is the same tree). Production approved. Sanjay's agent then reproduced bugs in bin/gp-pi that Jeff fixed in 7f76519: `recreate omni` destroys the container then dies on the overlap check, `rm --all` exits silently under set -e, a fixed host port collides across instances. Simulated from omni#3187 (ENG-11449), focused to its non-test source. attachMergedRaces re-reads head races with the caller's raceColumns select and joins them to the heads by row.id; when raceColumns omits id every join misses and is dropped by a silent continue, so places return Races: []. Production approved it; #3285 fixed it (ENG-11491).

Simulated from omni#2747, focused to its gp-api non-test source. smsComplianceWindow exempts only a record with kickoffSentAt or internalTestingAt, but kickoffSentAt shipped in May 2026, so approved legacy records have it null and are treated as past the 19-day cutoff, disabling SMS for compliant candidates. Fixed by #2888 (ENG-11326, ENG-11328).

Simulated from omni#2594, focused to its non-test source. The purchase webhook stamps the send's freeTextsApplied before redeemFreeTexts runs the campaign's one-time-offer CAS, so two concurrent eligible sends on one campaign can both be stamped while only one wins, and capture undercharges the loser by the free-texts discount (about $175). Production approved it; #2657 fixed it by stamping inside the CAS transaction.

Simulated from omni#2368 (19k lines), focused to the ingest service, its contracts, schema and queue consumer. Ingest reads IssueTag by (organizationSlug, normalizedName) and creates it when missing, so two synthesis runs in one org that propose the same theme both insert; the second hits the unique constraint, its whole ingest transaction rolls back, and the run stays running until the sweep fails it. The per-effort activeKey does not serialize runs across efforts. Production approved it; #2753 fixed it with createMany skipDuplicates and a re-read.

The new POST test-fixtures/vendor-mocks/outreach/:id/admin-actions route runs assertOutreachOwner, which 404s any outreach row with a null campaignId, while the same PR's applyOutreachAdminAction accepts null campaignId. Serve sends are org-scoped with campaignId null, so the route is dead for the Serve outreach it was built to drive. Production approved; ecf00407de fixed it.

Resending a payment-failed robocall runs convertDraft, which moves settleState from hold_failed to pending_payment before payment. If the candidate leaves the pay step, findByScope hides the row (it shows pending_payment only for a hold_failed robocall) and the cancel sweep only claims hold_failed rows, so the send vanishes from history and cannot be resent. Production approved; b1f7b4ae58 fixed it.

With WIN_SMS_HOLD_BILLING on, the hold path prices a free-texts-eligible P2P send (5,000 contacts or fewer) at the undiscounted amount, while SmsReviewStep still computes isFree and calls complete-free-purchase, which purchase.service rejects for a non-zero amount. The send can never go out. Production approved; dcd48fb923 (#2811) fixed it.

Production blocked on a multi-office org silently skipping a community issue in priorityOnboarding.service.ts. ElectedOffice.organizationSlug is @unique, so an org holds one office and the path cannot happen; the reviewer's own earlier run at this sha falsified the same lead. Nothing to block.

Production blocked claiming clerk-auth.service.test.ts would break because verifyToken now gets an options key set to undefined. Production blocked saying the Serve month grid in user_lookup_peer_grids.sql drops steps before serve_started_at. That is the documented intent: the model's yaml says the grid runs from the signup or Serve start month to today. Nothing to block.

Simulated from omni#3370 (171 files), focused to the contact-upload contract, the gp-api module and the webapp client that sends the file. The contract allows 25 MB files, and the browser posts them as multipart through the webapp's /api proxy on Vercel, which caps request bodies at 4.5 MB, so any file between 4.5 and 25 MB gets a 413 and a generic error. Annotation attachments at the base already presign and upload straight to S3. Production approved; ad42df28 fixed it with a presigned PUT.

Production blocked on record_fetch and record_head in packages/gp-ai/broker/page_replay.py blocking the event loop with boto3 calls. They are sync callables run as BackgroundTasks, and the Starlette the broker locks (1.3.1, uv.lock) sends sync callables to the threadpool. Nothing to block.

Production blocked on event_properties:activeproduct in int__amplitude_events_classified.sql not matching the camelCase activeProduct key. The : path on a JSON string column is case-insensitive in Databricks, which the author confirmed on the warehouse. Nothing to block.

Simulated. Modeled on INC-101, where a filter matching about 82,000 recipients outran the gateway during phone-list resolution. The new preview route drives resolveFilterAudience synchronously on the request path in pages of 1,000 up to the 200,000 cap, but unlike the build path (p2pPhoneListUpload.service.ts:854) and the Serve SMS create path it passes no timeBudgetMs. An audience of about 82,000 or more means 82+ sequential Databricks page reads inside one request, past the ~120 s gateway, so the official gets a gateway timeout instead of a count. docs/scale.md rows: Interactive resolution budget 90 s (gateway gives up at ~120 s); Known traps, per-page work over an audience on the request path.

Simulated. Modeled on the omni#3370 contact-upload match pipeline. The match input is one bound JSON string parameter, and Databricks caps a single parameter at 1,048,576 characters (stated in the util's comments and contactUploads/AGENTS.md), not at the 16 MiB statement size the diff sizes against. At a typical ~235 characters per row, a 20,000-row chunk is about 4.7M characters, so any upload over roughly 4,400 rows fails its match statement; uploads go up to 100,000 rows. docs/scale.md rows: Contact upload rows 100,000; Known traps, Match SQL input is capped at 800,000 chars (contactUploadMatchSql.util.ts:53).

Simulated. Modeled on the Serve SMS delivery path. findTextedSince passes every resolved person id as a Prisma `personId: { in: [...] }` list, and the resolved audience can hold up to 200,000 ids. Prisma fails above 32,767 bound values, so any Serve send to more than about 32,767 constituents throws in the frequency-cap lookup and the send never writes its CSV. docs/scale.md rows: Audience cap per resolution 200,000; Known traps, ids as bound parameters in Postgres fail above 32,767 values.

Simulated. Modeled on the door-knocking pack path that once held a ~21.5M-row statewide district in memory. The new pre-check is a single COUNT(*) row over the same FROM/WHERE the export uses, so it holds one aggregate regardless of district size, and anything over MAX_PACK_ROWS (3,000,000) is refused before the export starts. Nothing new is paged, held or bound per person, and the existing post-export check stays as a backstop. docs/scale.md rows: Door-knocking pack rows 3,000,000; Known traps, whole district held in memory.

Simulated. Modeled on the recipient caps listed in docs/scale.md (Audience cap per resolution 200,000; Peerly phone list recipients 200,000). The diff swaps a private 200,000 constant for the shared MAX_AUDIENCE_RECIPIENTS of the same value and rewrites two refusal messages. No query, loop, page size or cap value changes, so every path stays bounded exactly as before.

Simulated. Modeled on the outreach materialization path's OFFSET paging over captured phone-list recipients, which ran inside the launch request. The diff moves the captured-list write onto the existing SQS queue (a new outreachMaterialize message type with a per-outreach dedup id; the request only stamps the filter lock and enqueues) and replaces skip/take with keyset paging on the recipient id in pages of 10,000, stopping at MAX_AUDIENCE_RECIPIENTS (200,000). The largest list is 20 indexed reads and 20 createMany inserts with skipDuplicates, off the request path, so a redelivery is idempotent and nothing holds more than one page. A capture over the cap is logged rather than read. docs/scale.md rows: Outreach materialization page 1,000; Audience cap per resolution 200,000; Known traps, OFFSET paging re-sorts and skips everything before it, and per-page work over an audience on the request path.

Swaps the priority read to the MRP model with census tract as a dimension, one parameter per tract, fit synchronously inside gp-api's read-status request. The repo's ADR (docs/adr/2026-10-19-civic-panel-mrp-in-gp-api.md) sized it at a few dozen parameters and about 1 ms, and the PR body says speed on very large districts was not measured. Statewide North Carolina has 3,003 tracts; each read took 4 to 9 minutes on Node's one thread and froze the prod fleet on 2026-11-04 (post-mortem "Statewide read freeze"). Production approved with no findings. The fix (#3588) caps the model.

Adds the priority read (the per-tract MRP fit from #2977) to Home card sync, so every Home load runs it synchronously inside the request, with only a per-server cache. A large district's read takes minutes on Node's one thread, and the least-outstanding-requests balancer spreads repeat loads across servers until the fleet freezes (post-mortem "Statewide read freeze", 2026-11-04). The change is a small part of a 54-file PR. Production approved with no findings.

Adds the priority read-status call to the priority page's server render, so the page shows nothing until gp-api answers, and a failure or slow read takes the whole page with it. gp-webapp is a single-page app; this data should load client-side. On 2026-11-04 this is the path that sent seven read-status requests to six servers in 30 seconds (post-mortem "Statewide read freeze"). Production approved.
